book.title: Gluteal Tendinopathy and Greater Trochanteric Pain Syndrome

blocks.text: **Greater trochanteric pain syndrome (GTPS)** means pain over the outer (lateral) hip, centred on the **greater trochanter**, the bony point on the side of the hip. It is a descriptive label. In most patients the main source is now thought to be **gluteal tendinopathy**: a load-related problem of the gluteus medius and minimus tendons where they attach to the greater trochanter. These muscles are the main hip abductors and help keep the pelvis level when standing on one leg [Ref - to verify].
The older diagnosis of trochanteric bursitis is less often the main cause. A bursa may be irritated at the same time, but treating it alone is often not enough [Ref - to verify].

GTPS is most common in women over about 40 and in people with higher body weight, and it can also affect runners. It is often related to compression of the tendon against the bone when the hip is held in adduction (for example crossing the legs, lying on the side, standing with the weight on one hip) combined with load [Ref - to verify].

items: Pain on the outer hip that may spread down the outer thigh.
Pain when lying on the painful side at night, which often wakes the patient.
Pain with walking, stairs, getting up from a low chair, standing on one leg, and standing with the weight shifted on one hip.
Tenderness over the greater trochanter.
Usually no groin pain and no major loss of hip movement. If these are present, consider hip joint disease.

blocks.text: Honest note: gluteal tendinopathy is a clinical diagnosis. MRI or ultrasound can show tendon changes, but they are also common in people without symptoms, so imaging is used when the result will change management [Ref - to verify].
E1. Single-leg stance test

rows: Load the gluteal tendons in a compressive position to reproduce the familiar outer hip pain
Standing near a wall for safety, on the painful leg, with the other leg lifted
The patient stands on the painful leg for up to 30 seconds. Note the time at which pain starts and whether the pelvis drops
Reproduction of the familiar outer hip pain, often reported within about 30 seconds [Ref - to verify exact criteria]
A pain on single-leg stance with local tenderness supports gluteal tendinopathy
Not specific; also positive with other hip and lumbar problems [Ref - to verify]
Leaning the trunk toward the stance side to avoid load; allowing the lifted leg to touch the floor; stopping before 30 seconds without asking about pain
Use the time to pain as a baseline for monitoring

blocks.text: E2. Palpation of the greater trochanter

rows: Lying on the unaffected side with the painful hip slightly flexed, or supine
Press firmly on the greater trochanter and the lateral facet where the gluteus medius attaches
Localised tenderness that reproduces the familiar pain
GTPS; it is one of the most consistent findings
Local tenderness alone does not separate tendinopathy from bursitis or other lateral hip pain

blocks.text: E3. Resisted external derotation test

rows: Supine with the hip and knee at 90 degrees
Passively rotate the hip outward, then ask the patient to rotate the leg back toward the middle against the therapist's resistance
Gluteal tendinopathy, together with the other findings
Accuracy has been reported to vary; use with other tests [Ref - to verify]

blocks.text: E4. FABER (Patrick) test
The FABER position (flexion, abduction, external rotation) stretches the gluteal tendons and can reproduce lateral hip pain. Pain in the groin instead suggests a hip joint source. See Vol 7 Ch 1.
E5. Trendelenburg test and abductor strength

rows: Stand on one leg for 30 seconds and watch the pelvis from behind
The pelvis on the lifted side drops, or the trunk leans over the stance leg
Reduced hip abductor function; it is a sign of weakness or pain inhibition, not a diagnosis

blocks.text: E6. Ober test
The Ober test is not recommended as a diagnostic test for this condition because its validity is limited and it can aggravate the lateral hip [Ref - to verify].
E7. Outcome measures
VISA-G (Victorian Institute of Sport Assessment, gluteal) and a 0 to 10 pain scale, plus the time to pain on single-leg stance [Ref - to verify].

rows: Groin pain, reduced internal rotation, stiffness
Younger, groin pain with flexion and rotation
Outer knee more than hip, runners
Weakness, marked abductor loss, older women
Pain with impact, groin or lateral hip pain in runners
Tingling and numbness on the outer thigh, no weakness

sections.title: H. Working diagnosis and decision pathway

items: Any emergency or urgent flag? **Yes:** act as in Section G.

Lateral hip pain with greater trochanter tenderness, pain lying on that side, pain on single-leg stance or other compressive loading, full hip range without groin pain? **Yes:** working diagnosis is gluteal tendinopathy (GTPS).
Groin pain, stiffness or reduced internal rotation? **Yes:** use the hip joint pathway.
Back or neurological signs? Use the lumbar pathway.
Begin education, load management and progressive strengthening.
If there is no improvement after a full trial, review the diagnosis and consider imaging and medical options.

rows: Soft-tissue work to the gluteals, tensor fasciae latae and lumbar region
Gentle sustained pressure; avoid heavy pressure directly on the greater trochanter
Direct friction or stretching of the iliotibial band

blocks.text: **Preferred starting choice:** education, load management and exercise. Manual therapy is a minor adjunct. Do not use stretches that put the hip into adduction, such as the cross-body hip stretch, because they compress the tendon and may increase pain. Do not claim to release a tight iliotibial band.

sections.title: J. Exercise prescription (example starting plan, not universal)

blocks.text: **Principle:** education to reduce tendon compression, together with a progressive hip abductor strengthening program, has been shown to give better outcomes than waiting and than a corticosteroid injection at longer follow-up in at least one large trial [Ref - to verify]. A short-term benefit from injection occurs in some patients, but it may not last [Ref - to verify].
**Education to reduce compression (daily life):**

rows: Sit with the knees apart and the feet flat
Standing with the weight on one hip (hanging on the hip)
Stand with the weight on both feet
Sleeping on the painful side, or on the other side with the top leg dropping across
Sleep on the other side with a pillow between the knees, or on the back
Repeated stretching of the hip in adduction
Sudden increases in walking, hills, stairs or running
Isometric hip abduction against a wall or band, lying on the back
Press the outer leg into a wall or band in a neutral position, avoiding crossing the midline
5 holds of 30 to 45 seconds, once or twice a day [Ref - to verify]
Side-lying hip abduction, bridge, sit-to-stand, mini-squat with a band
Slow control, keep the hip out of adduction
Pain 3 to 4 out of 10 or less; easy
Control the pelvis, avoid hip drop
Good control and no next-day flare

blocks.text: **Symptom rule:** pain up to about 4 out of 10 that settles within 24 hours is acceptable [Ref - to verify]. Night pain and morning stiffness should not get worse. Increase load gradually.

**Return to running (example):** pain-free walking, good single-leg stance control, and tolerance of strength exercises at a moderate load. Start with short run-walk intervals and increase gradually. No fixed timeline is set.

rows: Option for persistent pain after several months of care

blocks.text: **Medical options (decided by doctors):** corticosteroid injection may reduce pain in the short term in some people, but repeated injections are not advised and long-term benefit is limited [Ref - to verify]. Other injections, and surgery for tears or persistent cases, are specialist decisions.

blocks.text: **Case:** A 54-year-old woman has 6 months of outer right hip pain that wakes her when lying on that side. She sits cross-legged and often stands with her weight on the right hip. Tenderness is over the right greater trochanter. Single-leg stance on the right causes pain at about 20 seconds. Hip range is full and painless, and the groin is not painful. No back or neurological findings, no red flags.

**Working diagnosis:** gluteal tendinopathy (GTPS). **Plan:** education on avoiding compression, isometrics, progressive hip abductor strengthening, graded walking, pillow between the knees at night, reassess every 3 to 4 weeks.
**Questions and answers**

items: Why avoid stretching the iliotibial band across the body? The stretch puts the hip into adduction and compresses the gluteal tendon against the bone, which may increase pain.
Why is the Ober test not used here? Its validity is limited, and it does not reliably identify the cause of lateral hip pain [Ref - to verify].
How do you separate GTPS from hip OA? GTPS has outer hip pain, trochanter tenderness and a full, painless hip range, while hip OA has groin pain and loss of internal rotation.
A runner has outer hip pain with impact and cannot hop. What do you suspect? A femoral neck stress fracture, so stop impact and refer for imaging urgently.
Why measure time to pain on single-leg stance? It is a simple, repeatable baseline that shows improvement in load tolerance.
**Initial approach:** education to reduce tendon compression, load management and progressive strengthening.
**Justifying findings:** outer hip pain, trochanter tenderness, single-leg stance pain, full hip range, no flags.
**Priority:** build tendon and abductor capacity while reducing compression.
**Manual therapy:** minor adjunct.
**Exercise:** isometrics, abductor strengthening, functional and graded load.
**Modalities:** limited role; shockwave for persistent cases.
**Tell the patient:** common and treatable; positions and load matter; recovery takes months.
**Avoid:** adducted stretches, lying on the painful side, deep friction, repeated steroid injections.
**Measure:** pain, single-leg stance time, VISA-G.
**If no improvement:** specialist review.
**Referral triggers:** Section G.
**Discharge:** function restored with a maintenance strength plan.

blocks.text: **Assumptions:** adult, no fracture or infection, normal hip range.

items: **Can be tested:** whether education plus exercise beats injection or waiting; whether shockwave adds benefit.
**Hypotheses:** that avoiding compression reduces tendon pain; that abductor strengthening improves tendon capacity.
**Future questions:** best exercise dose, and which patients benefit from injection or surgery.

blocks.text: Evidence not graded until references are verified.

sections.A: GTPS hip ke bahar ki taraf greater trochanter par dard hai, aksar gluteal tendons ki tendinopathy ki wajah se. Tendon par dabao (compression) is ko barhata hai.
sections.B: Hip ke bahar dard jo ran ke bahar tak ja sakta hai, usi taraf letne, ek taang par khade hone aur seerhiyan charhne se barhta hai.
sections.C: Dard bilkul kahan hai aur kya usi taraf let sakte hain.
sections.D: Chaal, pelvis ka girna, greater trochanter dabana aur single-leg stance.
sections.E: Yeh clinical diagnosis hai. MRI mein tendon ki tabdeeli bina dard wale logon mein bhi hoti hai. Single-leg stance 30 second ka test ahem hai.
sections.F: Hip OA (groin dard aur internal rotation kam), FAI aur kamar se aata dard isi jaise lag sakte hain.
sections.G: Runner ya kamzor haddi wale shakhs mein impact se dard (bone stress injury), ya girne ke baad fracture ka shak: refer.
sections.H: Red flags na hon, hip ke bahar dard, trochanter par dard aur single-leg stance par dard: gluteal tendinopathy.
sections.I: Gluteals aur TFL par soft tissue kaam se thori der ka aaraam.
sections.J: Sab se ahem: tendon ka dabao kam karna (taang cross na karna, side par letne ka tareeqa) aur abductor muscles ki dheere dheere barhti exercise.
sections.K: Barf, garmi aur TENS optional. Kai hafton ki exercise ke baad bhi dard rahe to shockwave.
sections.L: Hip, kamar aur SIJ screen karein, GTPS ko load aur dabao ka masla samjhayein, phir 8 se 12 hafte ki exercise.
sections.M: Dard, single-leg stance mein dard tak waqt, side par letne ka dard, VISA-G aur abductor taaqat dobara dekhein.
sections.N: 54 saal ki khatoon ko 6 mahine se usi taraf letne par hip dard se neend khulti hai. Khud socho, phir jawab dekho.
sections.chapter-summary-treatment-decision: Mukhtasar: tendon ka dabao kam karna, load control aur dheere dheere barhti exercise.
